subject: physics
title: Superposition and Young's Double Slit
welcome_lead: Stack waves on each other and decode the bright fringes of Young's classic experiment.
meta_desc: A-Level Waves adventure on superposition, interference and double-slit fringe spacing.
final_note: Path difference of n lambda gives a bright fringe; (n+½) lambda gives a dark one.

concepts.def: Resultant displacement is sum of individual ones.
w = lambda D / s for Young's slits.
Difference in distance from each source.

walkthroughs.body_html: When two waves overlap, total displacement equals the vector sum. Identical waves in phase double in amplitude (constructive); pi out of phase cancel (destructive).
Two coherent slits separated by s, screen distance D, light wavelength lambda. Bright fringes appear with spacing w = lambda D / s. Greater D or smaller s widens fringes.
Bright: path difference = n lambda. Dark: path difference = (n + 0.5) lambda. n is an integer (0,1,2,.).

mcqs.q: For Young's slits, fringe spacing w equals:
options: s D / lambda
lambda D / s
lambda s / D
D / (lambda s)

mcqs.q: Constructive interference requires path difference of:
options: (n+0.5) lambda
n lambda
lambda / 2
lambda / 4

mcqs.q: What is the formula for Young's modulus?
options: It is unchanged because the wave doesn't lose energy.
Stress / strain — the ratio in the linear (elastic) region of a stress-strain graph.
Extension / original length — the same as strain.
Force / area — the same as stress itself.

mcqs.q: When two waves interfere destructively, what happens to the energy?
options: Energy is destroyed at points of destructive interference.
Energy is redistributed — there is constructive interference elsewhere, conserving total energy.
Extension / original length — the same as strain.
Energy turns into mass according to E=mc^2 when waves cancel.

mcqs.q: If you double your distance from a point source of waves, what happens to the intensity?
options: It halves — intensity is inversely proportional to distance.
It falls to one quarter — intensity follows an inverse-square law with distance from a point source.
Extension / original length — the same as strain.
It is unchanged because the wave doesn't lose energy.
